questions.q: Let ${x}^{k} + {y}^{k} = {a}^{k}, \left(a, k > 0\right)$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = 0,$ then $k$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x$

$k . {x}^{k - 1} + k . {y}^{k - 1}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - {\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}^{k - 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + {\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)}^{k - 1} = 0$

$⇒ k - 1 = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ k = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q:
Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $(\sin x \cos y)(f(2 x+2 y)-f(2 x-2 y))=(\cos x\sin \mathrm{y})(f(2 \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y})+f(2 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{y}))$, for all $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \in \mathbf{R}$.
If $f^{\prime}(0)=\frac{1}{2}$, then the value of $24 f^{\prime \prime} \left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & (\sin x \cos y)(f(2 x+2 y)-f(2 x-2 y))=(\cos x \sin y) \\ & (f(2 x+2 y)+f(2 x-2 y)) \\ & f(2 x+2 y)(\sin (x-y))=f(2 x-2 y) \sin (x+y) \\ & \frac{f(2 x+2 y)}{\sin (x+y)}=\frac{f(2 x-2 y)}{\sin (x-y)} \\ & \text { Put } 2 x+2 y=m, 2 x-2 y=n \\ & \frac{f(m)}{\sin \left(\frac{m}{2}\right)}=\frac{f(n)}{\sin \left(\frac{n}{2}\right)}=\mathrm{K} \\ & \Rightarrow f(m)=K \sin \left(\frac{m}{2}\right) \\ & \therefore f(x)=K \sin \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{K}{2} \cos \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \\ & P_{\text {Put }} x=0 ; \frac{1}{2}=\frac{K}{2} \Rightarrow K=1 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{4} \sin \frac{x}{2} \\ & 4 f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)=\left(-\frac{1}{4} \sin \left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)\right) 24 \\ & =\frac{-24}{8}=-3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $x\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}cost\sqrt{sin2t}$ and $y \left($t\right) = 2$\sqrt{2}$sint$\sqrt{sin2t},$t \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right). Then \dfrac{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2}{d^{2}y{dx}^{2}} at $t = \dfrac{π}{4}$is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$x = 2\sqrt{2}cost\sqrt{sin2t}$

Now differentiating w.r.t~$t$~both side we get,

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}cos3t}{sin2t} . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given~$y\left(t\right) = $2\ssqrt{2}sint\sqrt{sin2t}$

Again differentiating w.r.t~$t$~both side we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}sin3t}{sin2t} . . . . . . \left($2\right)$

Now dividing equation~ \left($2\right)$~from~ \left($1\right)$~we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} =tan3t$

Now finding the value of~$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$~at $t = \dfrac{π}{4}$~we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -1$

Now finding~$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$~we get,

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\sec^{2}3t \cdot \sqrt{sin2t}}{cos3t}$

Now finding value of~$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$at $t = \dfrac{π}{4}$~we get,

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = -3$

Now putting the value of~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} \text{ and } \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$~$in\dfrac{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2}{d^{2}ydx^{2}}$~we get,

$\dfrac{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)2}{d^{2}ydx^{2}} = \dfrac{1 + 1}{- 3} = - \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: For $x > 1$, if \left(2x\right)2y = 4e^{2x - 2y}$, then \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}} ⁡ 2x\right)2\dfrac{dy}{dx}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,& \left(2x\right)2y = 4 . e^{2x - 2y}$

Taking~natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$2ylo{g}_{e}2x = lo{g}_{e}4 + \left(2x - 2y\right)$

$⇒ 2y = \left(\dfrac{lo{g}_{e}4 + 2x}{1 + lo{g}_{e}2x}\right)

Differentiating both sides with respect to~$x$, we get

\dfrac{2dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}2x\right) . 2 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}4 + 2x\right)\dfrac{1}{x}}{\left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}2x\right)2}~(Using quotient rule)

$⇒ \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}2x\right)2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(\dfrac{x . lo{g}_{e}2x - lo{g}_{e}2}{x}\right).$

$

questions.q: If $y ( x ) = \cot^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + sinx} + \sqrt{1 - sinx}}{\sqrt{1 + sinx} - \sqrt{1 - sinx}}\right), x \in \left(\dfrac{π}{2}, \pi\right), then \dfrac{dy}{dx} at $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$y ( x ) = \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} + \sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x}}{\sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} - \sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x}}$

As we know that,~$\sqrt{1 - sin ⁡ x} = \left|sin\dfrac{x}{2} - cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right| \text{ and } \sqrt{1 + sin ⁡ x} = \left|sin\dfrac{x}{2} + cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right|$

$y ( x ) = \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{\left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right| + \left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right|}{\left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right| - \left|cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}\right|}$

$= \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} - sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2} + cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}\text{for}x \in \left(\dfrac{π}{2}, \pi\right)

$= \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{sin ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}{cos ⁡ \dfrac{x}{2}}\right)$

$= \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \left($tan ⁡ $\dfrac{x}{2}\right)

$= \cot^{- 1} ⁡ \left(cot ⁡ ( \dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2} )\right)$

$y ( x ) = \dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2}$

$y^{′} ( x ) = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{2 \cos \theta+2 \cos ^2 \theta-1}{4 \cos ^3 \theta-3 \cos \theta+8 \cos ^2 \theta-4+5 \cos \theta+2} \\ & y=\frac{\left(2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta-1\right)}{\left(2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta-1\right)(2 \cos \theta+2)} \\ & y=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{1+\cos \theta}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=\frac{1}{2} \\ & y^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{-1}{(1+\cos \theta)^2} \times(-\sin \theta)\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} y^{\prime \prime} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\cos \theta(1+\cos \theta)^2-\sin \theta(2)(1+\cos \theta)(-\sin \theta)}{(1+\cos \theta)^4}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=1\end{aligned}$

The given equation can be written as

$y = \sin^{3} \left(\dfrac{π}{3}cosg \left($x\right)\right)$~

where,

g\left($x\right) = \dfrac{π}{3\sqrt{2}}\left(-4x^{3} + 5x^{2} + 1\right)3 / 2$

$⇒ g^{'} \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(-$4x^{3} + 5x^{2} + 1\right)1 / 2\left(-12x^{2} + 10x\right)$

$⇒ g^{'}\left(1\right) = $\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(-$2\right) = - \pi$

And,

$g \left(1\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \left(\pi - \dfrac{π}{3}\right)

Now,

$y^{'} = 3\sin^{2} $\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}$cosg \left(x\right)\right) \timescos $\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}$cosg \left($x\right)\right)$\times $\dfrac{π}{3}\left(-sing \left(x\right)\right)g^{'}\left(x\right)$

$y^{'}\left(1\right) = 3\sin^{2}\left(- $\dfrac{π}{6}\right) \cdotcos\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) \cdot \dfrac{π}{3}\lleft(-sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)g^{'} \left($1\right)$

$y^{'}\left($1\right) = $\dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{π}{3}\left(\dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(- \pi\right) = \dfrac{3{π}^{2}}{16}

y\left($1\right) = $\sin^{3}\left(\dfrac{π}}{3}cos\d$dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = - \dfrac{1}{8}

Therefore,

$2y^{'}\left($1\right) + 3{π}^{2}y\left($1\right) = 0$

$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$~be defined as~$f \left(x\right) = x^{3} + x - 5$.~If $g\left(x\right)$~is a function such that $f \left(g \left(x\right)\right) = x, ∀ x \in R$, then $g^{'}\left(63\right)$& is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Here,& $g \left(f \left($x\right)\right) = x$~as~f\left($x\right)$~and~$g \left(x\right)$~are inverse of each other.

Now,~$g^{'}\left(f\left(x\right)\right)f^{'}\left(x\right) = 1$

$⇒ g^{'} \left(f \left($x\right)\right) = $\dfrac{1}{f^{'}\left(x\right)} \ldots \left($i\right)$

Now~f\left($x\right) = 63 ⇒ x^{3} + x - 5 = 63$

$⇒ x^{3} + x - 68 = 0$

So~$x = 4$~satisfies the above equation

$g^{'} \left(63\right) = \dfrac{1}{f^{'} \left(4\right)}$~ from~\left(i\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{3\left(4\right)2 + 1} = \dfrac{1}{49}$

$

$x = sinϕ, {y}_{2} = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2sinϕcosϕ}{cos2ϕ}\right) = \tan^{- 1} ( tan2ϕ ) = 2ϕ = 2\sin^{- 1}x$

$\dfrac{d{y}_{1}}{d{y}_{2}} = \dfrac{d{y}_{1} / dx}{d{y}_{2} / dx} = \dfrac{1\left(1 + x^{2}\right) \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}}{2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}}$

questions.q: Let, $f: R \to R$ be a function such that $f\left(x\right) = x^{3} + x^{2}f '  \left(1\right) + xf '' \left($2\right) + f ''' \left($3\right), ∀ x \in \mathbb{R} .$~Then f\left($2\right) equals$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,& $f\left(x\right) = x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c$

$⇒ f ' \left(x\right) = 3x^{2} + 2ax + b$

$⇒ f '' \left(x\right) = 6x + 2a$

$⇒ f ''' \left(x\right) = 6$

According to the question,~

$a = f ' \left(1\right) = 3 + 2a + b ⇒ a + b = - 3 . . . \left(i\right)$

$b = f '' \left(2\right) = 12 + 2a ⇒ 2a - b = - 12 . . . \left(ii\right)$

$c = f ''' \left(3\right) ⇒ c = 6$

Solving equations \left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$, we get, $a = - 5 \text{ and } b = 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x^{3} - 5x^{2} + 2x + 6$

$∴ f\left(2\right) = 8 - 20 + 4 + 6 = - 2 .$

$

questions.q: If $y  \left(x\right) = x^{x}, x > 0$, then $y^{"}\left(2\right) - 2y^{'}\left(2\right) is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $y = x^{x}$

$⇒ ln \left(y\right) = xln \left($x\right)$

Differentiate both sides w.r.t.~$x$

\dfrac{1}{y} .$y ' = 1 + ln \left(x\right)$

$⇒ y ' = y \left(1 + lnx\right) . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

$⇒ y ' = x^{x}\left(1 + lnx\right)$

at~$x = 2 ⇒ y = 4$

So,~$y ' ( 2 ) = 4 \left($1 + ln2\right) . . . . . . . ( 2 )$

Now differentiate the equation \left($1\right)$,

$y " = y ' \left($1 + lnx\right) + $\dfrac{y}{x}

$⇒ y " ( 2 ) = y ' \left($1 + ln2\right) + 2$

$⇒ y " ( 2 ) - y ' ( 2 ) = y ' ( ln2 ) + 2$

$⇒ y " ( 2 ) - 2y ' ( 2 ) = \left($ln2 - 1\right)y ' ( 2 ) + 2$

$= 4 ( ln2 - 1 ) ( ln2 + 1 ) + 2$

$= $4\left($ln2\right)2 - 2$

$

questions.q: Let $f ( x ) = cos\left(2\tan^{- 1}sin\left(\cot^{- 1}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{x}}\right)\right), 0 < x < 1$. Then:

Put $x = \sin^{2}\theta, 0 < x < 1$

$sin\theta = \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ f \left($x\right) = cos \left(2\tan^{- 1} ( sin\theta )\right)$

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = cos \left($2\tan^{- $1}\sqrt{x}\right)

$= $\dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x}\right)}

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)\left(- 1\right) - \left(1 - x\right) \cdot 1}{\left(1 + x\right)2}

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{- 2}{\left(1 + x\right)2}

Multiply,~\left($1 - x\right)2$~on both sides

$⇒ \left($1 - x\right)2f^{'}\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{- 2\left(1 - x\right)2}{\left(1 + x\right)2}

Now, 2\lleft(f\left(x\right)\right)2 = \dfrac{2\left(1 - x\right)2}{\left(1 + x\right)2}$

$∴ \left(1 - x\right)2f^{'} \left(x\right) + $2\l$left(f\left($x\right)\right)2 = 0$~option \left($1\right) satisfied

$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = 2cos\theta - 2cos2\theta$

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{d\theta}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\dfrac{d\theta}{dx} = - \dfrac{3}{2}{cosec}^{2}\dfrac{3\theta}{2} . \dfrac{d\theta}{dx}$

$⇒ \left\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right|\theta = \pi = \dfrac{3}{4\left(- 1 - 1\right)} = \dfrac{3}{8}$

$Suppose $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left({2}^{x} + {2}^{- x}\right)tanx\sqrt{\tan^{- 1} \left(x^{2} - x + 1\right)}}{ \left($7x^{2} + 3x + 1\right)3}$. Then the value of $f^{'}\left($0\right)$ is equal to

$⇒ f^{'}\left(0\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left({2}^{h} + {2}^{- h}\right)tanh\sqrt{\tan^{- 1}\left(h^{2} - h + 1\right)}}{h\left(7h^{2} + 3h + 1\right)3}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(0\right) = \dfrac{\left({2}^{0} + {2}^{0}\right)\sqrt{\tan^{- 1}\left(1\right)}}{\left(0 + 1\right)3}$

questions.q: Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable functions on $R$ such that $fog$ is the identity function. If for some $a, b \in \mathbb{R}, g^{'}  \left(a\right) = 5$ and $g\left(a\right) = b,$ then $f^{'}\left(b\right) is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = x$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(g\left(x\right)\right) . g^{'}\left(x\right) = 1$

Put $x = a$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(g\left(a\right)\right)g^{'}\left(a\right) = 1$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(b\right) \times 5 = 1$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(b\right) = \dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.q: If& $2x^{y} + 3y^{x} = 20,$~then~$\dfrac{dy}{dx}$~at~  \left(2, 2\right)$& is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$2x^{y} + 3y^{x} = 20$

Now differentiating both sides w.r.t~$x,$~we get

$2x^{y}\left(y^{'}lnx + \dfrac{y}{x}\right) + 3y^{x}\left(lny + \dfrac{x}{y} \cdot y^{'}\right) = 0$~\left\{\text{here}ln = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\right\}$

Putting~$x = 2 \text{ and } y = 2,$~we get

$⇒ 8\left(ln2 \cdot y^{'} + 1\right) + 12\left(lny + y^{'}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 8\left(ln2 \cdot y^{'} + 1\right) + 12 \left($lny + y^{'}\right) = 0$

$⇒ y^{'} = - \left(\dfrac{3ln2 + 2}{2ln2 + 3}\right)

$⇒ y^{'} = - \left(\dfrac{2 + ln8}{3 + ln4}\right)$

$

questions.q: Let $f: S \to S$ where $S = \left($0, $\infty\right) be a twice differentiable function such that $f \left(x + 1\right) = xf \left(x\right)$. If $g: S \to R$ be defined as $g \left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}f \left(x\right)$, then the value of \left|g^{''}\left(5\right) - g^{''}\left(1\right)\right|$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$lnf \left(x + 1\right) = ln \left(xf \left(x\right)\right)$

$lnf \left(x + 1\right) = lnx + lnf \left(x\right)$

$⇒ g \left($x + 1\right) = lnx + g \left($x\right)$

$⇒ $g\left($x + 1\right) - g ( x ) = lnx$

$⇒ g^{''}\left($x + 1\right) - g^{''}\left($x\right) = - \dfrac{1}{x2}$

Put $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$

$g^{''} \left($2\right) - g^{''} \left($1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{12} . . . \left(1\right)$

$g^{''} \left(3\right) - g^{''} \left(2\right) = - \dfrac{1}{22} . . . \left(2\right)$

$g^{''} \left(4\right) - g^{''} \left(3\right) = - \dfrac{1}{32} . . . \left(3\right)$

$g^{''} \left($5\right) - g^{''} \left($4\right) = - \dfrac{1}{42} . . . \left(4\right)$

Add all the equations~we get

$g^{''}\left($5\right) - g^{''}\left($1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{22} - \dfrac{1}{32} - \dfrac{1}{42}$

\left|$g^{"}\left($5\right) - g^{"}\left($1\right)\right| = \dfrac{205}{144}

$

questions.q: If $y\left(x\right) = \left(x^{x}\right)x, x > 0$~then $\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}} + 20$~at $x = 1$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$y\left(x\right) = \left(x^{x}\right)x$

Taking $\log_{\mathrm{e}}$ both side

$lny\left(x\right) = x^{2} \cdot lnx$

Now differentiating both side w.r.t~$x$~we get,

$\dfrac{1}{y\left(x\right)} \cdot y^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x2}{x} + 2x \cdot lnx$

$y^{'} \left(x\right) = y \left($x\right)\left[x + 2xlnx\right]$~.......(i)

Given~$y\left(1\right) = 1$, so~$y^{'}\left(1\right) = 1$

Now rewriting~equation (i) again we get,

\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1}{x^{x^{2} + 1}\left(1 + 2lnx\right)}

Now~\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\left($x^{x^{2} + 1}\left(1 + 2lnx\right)\right)- 1\$right)\dfrac{dx}{dy}

$⇒ $\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}} = \dfrac{- x^{x2}\left(1 + 2lnx\right)\left(x^{2} + 3 + 2x^{2}lnx\right)}{ \l$left(x^{x2} \left($1 + 2lnx\right)\right)3}$ \times1$

$⇒ $\$left(\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}}\right)$x = 1 = - 4$

So,~ \left(\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}}\right)$x = 1 + 20 = - 4 + 20 = 16

$

Hence,~f\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{2 \cdot {2}^{x}}{1 + {2}^{2x}}
